subject: Private deployment — delineation of tenant control, operator privileges, and CMK handling
messages:
From: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify data access + keys for private deployment (Acme Health)

Marcus,

Thanks for the excellent demo last week. As we scope the Private deployment (VPC + on-prem connectors) for Acme, legal/security asked me to get written confirmation on a few points so we can include them in the DPA annex. High level asks:

- Customer-managed keys: we need confirmation that Acme will be able to supply and control the KMS keys (CMK) used to encrypt runtime secrets and KV cache, and that Redwood operators do not possess the plaintext keys.
- Operator privileges: we need a clear statement of what Redwood staff can and cannot access in the Private deployment — specifically whether any operator processes ever see plaintext model inputs/outputs or cached tokens.
- Subprocessors & transfers: we need an up-to-date list of subprocessors and any scenarios where data might cross borders (EU regulator concern).

Could you send a short note we can forward to our counsel + SOC2 reviewers? Preferably with proposed DPA language or annex we can add. Also tell me if you have an internal break-glass / emergency access playbook for support incidents that require operator intervention.

Thanks,
Bethany
Bethany Cho
Head of Security Operations, Acme Health
bethany.cho@acmehealth.com

Attachment: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify data access + keys for private deployment (Acme Health)

Bethany —

Great questions, and glad the demo was useful. Short answer: yes, we support customer-managed keys in Private deployments and we can commit to a narrow operator access model; below is a concise summary you can share with counsel. I'll follow up with a DPA annex draft attached.

1) Customer-managed keys (CMK)
- Deployment model: Acme can configure a customer KMS endpoint in your VPC (bring-your-own-key). Keys are used to envelope-wrap runtime secrets (API tokens, TLS certs) and to encrypt persistent KV cache at rest.
- Operational detail: Redwood runtime will receive only encrypted blobs; decryption happens on instances with access to the CMK inside your VPC. Redwood's control-plane has no persistent plaintext keys.

2) Operator privileges and telemetry
- Normal operations: Redwood operators have access to aggregated telemetry (latency, errors, token counts) and non-identifying logs.
- No-plaintext guarantee: Operator processes and staff are not authorized to access decrypted model inputs/outputs or unwrapped KV cache. Engineering break-glass requires an explicit legal & customer authorization workflow (see playbook below).

3) Break-glass / emergency access
- Mechanism: emergency access is strictly role-based, time-limited, and requires: (a) customer approval via a signed authorization or DocuSign; (b) an incident ticket in our tracked system; (c) legal review for requests involving content. Access is logged and recorded for audit.

4) Subprocessors & transfers
- Typical subprocessors: public cloud provider for control-plane (metadata only), observability vendor (aggregated telemetry), and a CDNI for software updates. I attached a current subprocessor matrix in case your legal team wants the list.

I've attached a draft Annex A with suggested DPA language we can iterate on. If you want, Kim (cc'd) from our Privacy team can formalize the text for legal.

Proposed next step: I can add the proposed wording to DocuSign (link will include a tracked addendum) once you confirm the phrasing below.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Product — Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: draft_dpa_annex_A_v3.pdf

From: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify data access + keys for private deployment (Acme Health)

Marcus — thanks. A couple of follow-ups from our security architects and legal: 

- Subprocessor detail: can you enumerate the exact subprocessors (not just categories) and the role they play? Our counsel will want to confirm contractual limits and data routing controls.
- KV cache & model state: when you say "KV cache encrypted at rest", can you confirm whether the runtime ever populates a plaintext cache in memory that an operator process could snapshot? We need assurance that no operator-facing syscall or debug hook exposes plaintext tokens.
- Key wrapping: is the envelope/dek wrapping performed inside our VPC only, and does Redwood ever receive wrapped keys outside the VPC? Please be explicit.

Separately — if there's any chance logs or traces include partial PII or PHI, we need the retention window and a sample retention policy. Acme is concerned about EU patients' data crossing into US control plane.

If you can send answers we can forward to legal.

Bethany

From: Irene Choi <irene.cho@redwoodinference.com>
To: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify data access + keys for private deployment (Acme Health)

Bethany / Marcus —

Adding a legal & compliance perspective. Below are two options we can propose in the annex; both are conservative and intended to satisfy regulated health data concerns. Please comment which is preferable for Acme counsel.

Option A (restrictive):
- Operator privileges: "Redwood personnel shall not access or possess plaintext customer inputs, outputs, tokens, or KV caches in Private deployments unless Customer grants explicit written authorization for a specific incident. Any such access shall be time-limited, recorded, and subject to customer review."
- Key custody: "Customer holds sole custody of CMKs used to envelope-wrap data; Redwood does not hold key material."
- Escrow: optional key escrow with neutral third party under court order only.

Option B (operational flexibility):
- Same as A, but permits Redwood to perform ephemeral in-scope debug actions in a hardened environment under joint customer/Redwood supervision and with a pre-specified SLA for notification and post-incident report.

Subprocessors: I attached the current matrix with provider names and roles. Note that the control plane (metadata-only) resides on our US tenant; for EU-heavy customers we can route control-plane telemetry to EU regions under contract.

Attachment: subprocessor_matrix_20270408.csv

Happy to craft the formal clause; Marcus / Kim, can you pick which option Acme prefers?

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
irene.cho@redwoodinference.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.cho@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify data access + keys for private deployment (Acme Health)

Bethany —

Thanks — and appreciate the precision from your team. Quick answers inline and a proposed operational flow below you can share with counsel: 

- Subprocessors (explicit): Control-plane provider: RedCloud Inc. (metadata only), Observability: PulseMetrics Ltd. (aggregated telemetry), SW distribution: CDNCo. We will include contract excerpts in the matrix.

- KV cache / memory: runtime keeps KV cache encrypted at rest; when the process decrypts entries to serve a request, decryption happens on customer-controlled instances inside the VPC using the CMK. Those in-memory plaintext windows are minimized and not written to disk. Operator-level access to instance memory is not part of normal support; any snapshotting requires break-glass authorization.

- Key wrapping flow: DEK generated per-node; envelope-wrapped by customer CMK inside your KMS. Wrapped DEKs may transit Redwood control-plane for orchestration but remain cryptographically sealed; only nodes in your VPC can unwrap.

Operational playbook (proposed):
1) Incident detection triggers a support ticket with Acme.
2) If operator access to plaintext is requested, Redwood requests signed authorization (DocuSign link) + legal approval.
3) Access window is limited to X hours, recorded with session capture and audit trail, and followed by a post-incident report.

I've prepared a DPA addendum draft that matches Option A language and added the subprocessors list. If that works, we can send the DocuSign package for Acme Counsel to sign: https://docusign.example.com/Acme-DPA-Addendum-12345

Attachment: dpa_addendum_proposed.docx

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify data access + keys for private deployment (Acme Health)

Marcus / Irene / Kim —

This looks good and addresses the biggest concerns. A couple of final asks from counsel before we route to signature: 

- Please add an explicit sentence that operator telemetry is metadata-only (no payloads or partial inputs), and that model weights and KV cache remain encrypted and are not exported to Redwood control plane in plaintext.
- In the break-glass flow, note that Acme may require that a Redwood engineer be present in a joint session (screen-share) while the operation is performed; we want the customer to be able to supervise any unwrapping/decryption.

If you add those two lines to the annex I will share with our counsel and get this queued for signature. Once legal signs we can schedule the Private deployment runbook work with your Solutions team.

Please put the final text in the DocuSign package and share a link.

Best,
Bethany
Bethany Cho
Head of Security Operations, Acme Health

Attachment: none
